approach: Parameterise the one history check's exempt source: add check_history_with_exempt(git, tip, Option<Vec<String>>); check_history calls it with None. New module legacy.rs holds a builder (athena.toml's [history] exempt list plus a const reason table copied from the athena.toml comments, giving a validated LegacyExempt record and a Change for legacy-exempt.json, writing nothing), a reader of legacy-exempt.json at the records tip, check_legacy(git, c0) (runs check_history_with_exempt on C0 with the list from the records tip), and check_attribution_with_legacy(git, main_tip, now, c0) (legacy check, then the part 1 walk starting after C0 via an inner fn with an optional cutover; check_attribution passes None). Append-only is enforced by the existing RecordsWriter::append and audit_history; tests prove it for legacy-exempt.json, and a legacy-specific finding covers a records history where that file changed. C0 is only an argument; no CLI or CI wiring.

decisions.choice: Add check_history_with_exempt with an optional override that only replaces HistoryState.exempt; check_history delegates with None.
decisions.reason: HistoryState.exempt is the single place the walk reads the exempt list, so only the list differs (criterion 6).

rejected.option: Rewrite athena.toml in a synthetic tip config
rejected.why: The tip config also feeds the secrets and personal-data allow-lists, which must stay from the tip.

decisions.choice: Refactor check_attribution into an inner fn with an optional cutover; with a cutover the walk starts after C0 on main's first-parent line. Public signature unchanged.
decisions.reason: Post-C0 commits keep the part 1 rule; commits up to C0 are never judged by attribution.

rejected.option: Run the old walk from base and filter findings by position
rejected.why: Pre-C0 commits would still be judged and counted.

decisions.choice: Report legacy violations as AttributionReport findings of new FindingKinds (LegacyHistory, LegacyExemptMissing, LegacyExemptChanged), carrying the original Violation text; check_legacy also returns the raw HistoryReport.
decisions.reason: One report type; tests can compare violations with check_history's.

rejected.why: Callers would have to merge two reports.

decisions.choice: Keep reasons in a const table keyed by sha prefix, copied from the athena.toml comments; the builder errors on an entry with no reason.
decisions.reason: Comments can't be parsed reliably; an unknown entry fails loudly rather than getting an empty reason.

rejected.option: Parse athena.toml comments at run time

decisions.choice: Leave records_branch.rs and invariant.rs behaviour unchanged unless a gap appears; add tests only.
decisions.reason: RecordsWriter already refuses different bytes at an existing path and audit_history flags changed paths.

rejected.option: Special legacy-exempt guard in the writer
rejected.why: The general rule already covers it.

files.purpose: Legacy rule: reason table, record builder, records-tip reader, check_legacy, check_attribution_with_legacy, tests.
Add check_history_with_exempt; check_history delegates with None.
Inner walk with optional cutover; new finding kinds; module doc updated.
Small LegacyExempt helper (shas()) and test; no format change.
Record the legacy rule and builder.
Section 10 job 5: legacy rule built, C0 caller-supplied, record built but not written.

steps: Read testutil helpers and exemption tests in history.rs; add check_history_with_exempt and make check_history call it with None.
In attribution.rs add finding kinds and labels, factor the walk into an inner fn with an optional cutover, keep check_attribution as the None wrapper, and rewrite the module doc.
In athena-data history.rs add LegacyExempt::shas() and a test.
Create legacy.rs: reason table, legacy_exempt_record, read_legacy_exempt, check_legacy, check_attribution_with_legacy, with docs citing section 4 and D111 and saying C0 is caller-supplied.
Add pub mod legacy to lib.rs.
Write tests: seven names x present/absent, append-only refusal with unchanged bytes, changed-history finding, post-C0 and at-C0, builder with seven entries and no ref written.
Run cargo fmt --all, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: check_history at C0 also runs secrets and RecordSet::load with C0's athena.toml, so config problems surface as legacy violations.
risks.mitigation: This is today's logic unchanged by design; tests use constructed repos with a valid built-in config.

risks.risk: The seven reasons drift from the athena.toml comments.
risks.mitigation: The builder test asserts the exact seven shas and non-empty reasons; unknown entries error.
Inner fn takes cutover: Option<&str>; None keeps the old path; existing tests are not edited.

risks.risk: Test repos can't use the real shas.
risks.mitigation: Entries name the real sha of a constructed hand-change commit; the table keys on the seven names for reasons only.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests over the seven names: a small repo where a hand-change commit stands for each name. With the entry present in a legacy-exempt record, check_legacy with C0 at or after it reports no violation for the commit. With the entry absent, the violations equal check_history_with_exempt(git, c0, Some(vec![])) and check_history on an empty-exempt config.
demonstrations.observes: Seven present-entry tests pass with no violation; seven absent-entry tests show the same violation as today's check_history.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the override or the records read, present-entry tests report the governed-content violation, and the absent-entry equality fails.

demonstrations.method: Real-repo test: RecordsWriter::append the builder's record, then append a record with one more entry at legacy-exempt.json. Assert RecordsError::Refused, the tip unchanged and the blob bytes equal to the original. A second test with a forced changed history yields a LegacyExemptChanged finding.
demonstrations.observes: The refusal error is returned, the tip and bytes are unchanged, and the changed-history case gives a finding.
demonstrations.fails_without: If append accepted changed bytes, the second append would succeed and the unchanged-bytes assertion would fail.

demonstrations.method: Tests with c0 as an argument. (a) History base..C0..X with X unattributed: an Unattributed finding for X, none for pre-C0 commits, and checked counts only post-C0 commits. (b) C0 itself is a hand change: a legacy finding with the entry absent, excused with it present, and no Unattributed finding for it.
demonstrations.observes: Post-C0 unattributed commit gives FindingKind::Unattributed; pre-C0 commits give no attribution findings; the C0 commit follows the legacy verdict.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the walk started from the earliest intent's base, pre-C0 commits would be judged by attribution; if C0 were excluded from the legacy range, the C0 hand change would go unjudged.

demonstrations.method: Call the builder with builtin_config().history.exempt. Assert exactly seven expected shas, non-empty reasons, validate() Ok, and that resolve_tip on refs/heads/athena/records is still Missing in a fresh repo.
demonstrations.observes: len == 7, non-empty reasons, validate Ok, no ref created.
demonstrations.fails_without: An empty or short list, a missing reason (builder errors) or a branch write would fail the assertions.

demonstrations.method: Run clippy, then cargo fmt --check, on the finished change. Clippy is also run with -D warnings, as Athena's check does.
demonstrations.observes: Clippy emits no warnings and fmt --check reports no diff. Both exit 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unused function, unused finding kind or unformatted code in legacy.rs, attribution.rs or history.rs would make clippy -D warnings or fmt --check exit non-zero.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff: check_history reduced to a call to check_history_with_exempt(..., None), only the exempt initialiser changed, no walk copy in legacy.rs. Then run the existing history tests unchanged with cargo test -p athena-gate history.
demonstrations.observes: Existing history tests pass without edits; the diff touches no test bodies.
demonstrations.fails_without: A copied walk would show as duplicated code in legacy.rs, and a behaviour change would fail existing history tests.

demonstrations.method: Check that the diff lists no athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow file. Grep legacy.rs and attribution.rs for any const or fn that picks a C0. Read the module docs for the caller-supplied C0 statement and the section 4 and D111 citations.
demonstrations.observes: Only the deliverable files appear; no C0 chooser; docs cite section 4 and D111 and state C0 is a parameter.
demonstrations.fails_without: A governance edit would show in the diff stat; a hard-coded C0 would show in grep.

demonstrations.method: Read the head of attribution.rs in the diff.
demonstrations.observes: The sentence saying the legacy rule will come later is replaced by a description of check_attribution_with_legacy, its inclusive C0 parameter, and the records-only walk for later commits.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the doc unchanged, the diff would show no edit to the module doc and the old 'will come later' text would remain.
